title: Literal email states
brief: Absent, blank and present are three different states. A record lies once you flatten them into two.
instructions: Report literal NULL as missing, a literal empty string as empty, and every other input as value. Do not trim anything.
Return only the declared columns, in their declared order and exact SQL types, and follow the stated ordering contract. NULL placement is declared, not assumed.
starterExplanation: The starter reads customer_id and email out of customers. It runs. It does not answer the question.

hints.text: CASE, with an explicit test for absence: NULL is equal to nothing, not even itself.
Ask whether the value is missing before you ask whether it is empty.
Customer 10001 holds empty text; customer 10002 holds nothing at all.

dataClaims.sql: SELECT (count(*) FILTER (WHERE customer_id = 10001 AND email = ''))::VARCHAR || '/' || (count(*) FILTER (WHERE customer_id = 10002 AND email IS NULL))::VARCHAR FROM customers
dataClaims.claim: brief and hints[2]: customer 10001 holds empty text and customer 10002 holds NULL
